subject: Automotive & EVs
title: How Hydrogen Fuel Cells Work
description: A quick win: understand How Hydrogen Fuel Cells Work.

hook.text: A hydrogen fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen to produce electricity—and the only exhaust is water.

buildup.text: Hydrogen enters one side, oxygen from the air enters the other, and a membrane generates electric current.

discovery.text: That electricity powers an electric motor, making a fuel cell vehicle technically a type of electric car.

twist.text: Unlike batteries, fuel cells don't store energy—they generate it on demand from hydrogen in a pressurized tank.

climax.text: Refueling takes about five minutes, giving hydrogen a speed advantage over battery charging.

punchline.text: Hydrogen cars run on the universe's simplest element and emit only water.

quiz.question: What is the only byproduct of a hydrogen fuel cell?

details.summary: A hydrogen fuel cell generates electricity by combining hydrogen gas with oxygen in a chemical reaction that produces only water vapor as exhaust, powering an electric motor.
details.whyItMatters: Fuel cells offer the range and refueling speed of gasoline cars with zero tailpipe emissions, making them a compelling option for trucks and long-distance travel.
takeaways: Hydrogen reacts with oxygen across a membrane to produce electricity
The only byproduct is water vapor
Refueling takes about five minutes compared to hours for battery EVs

faq.question: Why haven't fuel-cell cars replaced battery EVs?
faq.answer: Hydrogen infrastructure is expensive and sparse, and producing green hydrogen costs more than grid electricity. Battery EVs benefit from a vast existing electrical grid and simpler refueling at home.

faq.question: Is hydrogen safe to use as a vehicle fuel?
faq.answer: Hydrogen is flammable but disperses rapidly in open air. Modern fuel tanks use carbon-fiber composites tested to withstand crashes and gunfire, making them comparable in safety to gasoline tanks.
